name: Orbit AI - Phase 6 - Onboarding provisioning automation (W6.3)

nodes.name: Provisioning webhook
nodes.notes: W6.3: 'Post-payment event... Auto (internal, reversible provisioning).' Fire-and-forget caller: a fourth parallel branch off stripe-payment-to-crm.workflow.json's 'Advance Opportunity to Won' node (wired this pass), alongside 'Respond: handled' and 'Track opening-line outcome'. Input: {companyId, opportunityId, companyName}. 'Reversible' per the brief's own gate label: a Drive folder and a PIN can both be deleted/regenerated by a human with no lasting harm, unlike a billing/contract action - consistent with why this is auto-execute, not human-gated, under the standing automation risk boundary.

nodes.name: Create Drive folder
nodes.notes: Real Google Drive API v3 shape (POST /files with mimeType:'application/vnd.google-apps.folder' is the documented way to create a folder, ?fields=id,webViewLink limits the response to what's actually needed) - not guessed, but UNVERIFIED against a live account. Uses a raw httpRequest call rather than n8n's native Google Drive node deliberately: that node's own parameter/UI shape varies enough across n8n versions that a raw REST call against Drive's stable public API is the safer bet here, same reasoning Stripe's signature verification uses a Code node over a native Stripe node. CREDENTIAL GAP, flagged: 'Google Drive OAuth2' is a distinct n8n OAuth2 credential from the gcloud CLI login command-center/src/vendors.ts already lists for the Google Cloud row (Application Default Credentials, not an OAuth2 client n8n's HTTP node can use) - a real Drive-scoped OAuth2 client needs to be created separately in Google Cloud Console and added to n8n; vendors.ts doesn't cover this yet. GOOGLE_DRIVE_CLIENTS_PARENT_FOLDER_ID is a new env var, not previously used anywhere in this repo.

nodes.name: Generate access PIN
nodes.notes: Same hash-not-plaintext discipline portal/netlify/functions/lib/verifyDocumentsPin.ts's own comments describe: only pinHash gets written onto the Company record below. plaintextPin is carried forward ONLY to the Activity Event log and the alert two nodes down - a deliberate tradeoff, not an oversight, see those nodes' own notes.

nodes.name: Write Company provisioning fields

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ driveFolderId: ($('Create Drive folder').item.json.data || $('Create Drive folder').item.json).id, driveFolderUrl: ($('Create Drive folder').item.json.data || $('Create Drive folder').item.json).webViewLink, documentsAccessPinHash: $json.pinHash }) }}

nodes.notes: New fields this pass, CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's Company object. driveFolderUrl is what portal/netlify/functions/lib/verifyDocumentsPin.ts returns to a client on a correct PIN - the whole point of W1.7's 'documented only, blocked on the folder not existing' gap, closed now that this workflow creates the folder for real.

nodes.name: Log PIN to Activity Event

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ opportunityId: $('Provisioning webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId, type: 'DocumentsAccessPinGenerated', pin: $('Generate access PIN').item.json.plaintextPin, at: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: DELIBERATE TRADEOFF, flagged: the plaintext PIN lands in the CRM's Activity Event timeline (and the alert below) even though the Company record itself only ever stores a hash. This is what lets a rep actually relay the PIN to the client (phone call, a manually-composed email - this workflow doesn't send one itself, see the alert node's own notes on why) without this workflow needing to make an external-send policy decision. It does mean anyone with CRM/Command-Center access can read a client's document PIN - acceptable for a low-stakes document-folder gate, not something to reuse for anything higher-stakes without reconsidering this tradeoff.

nodes.name: Alert: onboarding provisioned

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'info', source: 'onboarding-provisioning', message: $('Provisioning webhook').item.json.body.companyName + ' is provisioned - Drive folder created, documents PIN ' + $('Generate access PIN').item.json.plaintextPin + ' (relay to the client however makes sense - this workflow does not send it).', linkUrl: (($('Create Drive folder').item.json.data || $('Create Drive folder').item.json).webViewLink) }) }}

nodes.notes: Routes to #onboarding (alertRouting.ts matches 'onboarding' in the source string). This is the 'a human decides how/whether to relay it to the client' half of the PIN-handling tradeoff above - the automation's job ends at generating and surfacing the PIN internally, deliberately not building an auto-email-to-client flow, which would be an external send needing the same human-review gate every other client-facing draft in this repo goes through (nurture, CX, portal-abandonment) - simplest to just not build that path at all for a one-time operational PIN.
